title: Safety Incident Log Form
subtitle: Use this log to record events in sequence, reconcile sources, identify trends and exceptions, and transfer the last known status for a safety incident workflow.
description: An original operational safety incident log form that controls a workplace safety event and corrective-action record from identity and routing through evidence, qualified decision, exception management, implementation, handoff, and final verification.
use_case: Use when the reporting worker, supervisor, or incident coordinator needs a traceable log so the qualified safety, occupational health, operations, or regulatory reviewer can stabilize, investigate, classify, notify, correct, reopen work, or escalate the safety event under the emergency procedure, hazard-control plan, incident-investigation process, reporting rules, and anti-retaliation policy without relying on an informal email, spreadsheet, or unreviewed narrative.

sections.title: Safety Incident log period, ownership, and control
sections.guidance: Open a bounded log with a clear owner, source record, entry standard, and review cadence.

blocks.label: Safety Incident identity
Log ownership and routing
Log period and entry control

sections.title: Safety Incident baseline, entry rules, and expected evidence
sections.guidance: Define the expected operating state so each log entry can be interpreted later.

blocks.label: Safety Incident log-entry requirements
items: Emergency services, first aid, medical evaluation, or evacuation need is addressed
Immediate hazard is isolated and affected area controlled
People are accounted for and qualified support is notified
Event time, location, task, equipment, material, and operating state are captured
Photographs, video, physical items, alarms, logs, and system data preserve provenance
Reporter and witness accounts are collected separately and without coaching
Exposure, injury, illness, or symptom information is routed confidentially
Potential recurrence and similarly exposed work are identified
Investigation considers systemic and root causes rather than worker blame
Corrective actions include owner, due point, interim control, and effectiveness test
Qualified reviewer makes recordability and external-notification decisions
Work restart and closeout require evidence that controls are effective

blocks.label: Supporting evidence and source records
items: Initial report, emergency response, and notification timeline
Scene, equipment, control, material, and environmental photographs
Reporter, witness, supervisor, and responder factual accounts
Procedure, permit, training, inspection, maintenance, and prior-event records
Alarm, sensor, access, vehicle, production, or system log
Hazard isolation, medical-routing, and exposure-control reference
Cause analysis and corrective-action verification
Qualified reporting decision, restart authorization, and worker communication

blocks.label: Opening status, carried items, data sources, known gaps, entry conventions, and review assumptions

sections.title: Safety Incident recurring event log
sections.guidance: Enter events in sequence and preserve actor, result, source, and next action.

blocks.label: Safety Incident event and status log
Decision, correction, status change, reason, and authorization log
Sequence context, corrected entry, source conflict, missing interval, and interpretation limit

sections.title: Safety Incident trend, reconciliation, and period review
sections.guidance: Reconcile the log to source systems and identify patterns that require a decision or corrective action.

blocks.label: Population, source count, log count, variance, owner, and resolution
Period review and decision checks
items: Emergency needs and continuing hazards were addressed before routine investigation
Event time, location, task, people, equipment, material, and conditions are factual
Affected area, product, equipment, and worker population are bounded
Evidence preserves original condition, source, date, and custodian
Worker and witness accounts are distinguished from investigator conclusions
Analysis considers equipment, procedure, training, supervision, environment, and organizational factors
Corrective actions target underlying causes rather than blame alone
Action priority reflects potential severity and likelihood of recurrence
Work restart has a qualified authority, prerequisite, and verification
Recordkeeping and external-reporting decisions cite the applicable reviewer and basis

blocks.label: Period review outcome
Observed pattern, comparison basis, outlier, source limitation, operational effect, and decision need

sections.title: Safety Incident unresolved event and escalation register
sections.guidance: Preserve exceptions separately from routine entries until final disposition.

blocks.label: Log stop and escalation boundary
blocks.guidance: Pause any action outside documented authority. Protect privacy, preserve the original evidence, and route urgent, safety, security, retaliation, or legal concerns to the qualified safety, occupational health, operations, or regulatory reviewer under the emergency procedure, hazard-control plan, incident-investigation process, reporting rules, and anti-retaliation policy.

blocks.label: Safety Incident exception and escalation triggers
items: Fatality, emergency, severe injury, hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss may require immediate external review
Continuing energy, chemical, biological, fire, structural, traffic, or violence hazard exists
Multiple workers, visitors, contractors, or public members may be affected
Exposure boundary, involved material, equipment status, or scene integrity is uncertain
Evidence could be lost through cleanup, repair, restart, or digital overwrite
Similar event, near miss, or unclosed corrective action occurred previously
Reporter raises retaliation, intimidation, suppression, or reporting-access concern
Work restarted or control was removed without the required authorization

blocks.label: Exception, immediate action, owner, due point, and disposition register
Exception facts, affected scope, privacy boundary, unresolved risk, and escalation rationale

sections.title: Safety Incident period handoff and log closeout
sections.guidance: Transfer the last known status, open actions, and next required review to the receiving owner.

blocks.label: Log outcome and handoff
Open safety incident action and limitation register
Closeout and recipient handoff confirmations
items: Final decision and effective boundary are recorded
Evidence supporting the outcome is linked and readable
Every unresolved action has an owner and due point
Sensitive information is routed only to the designated restricted record
Affected people and receiving systems received the necessary status
Conditions, limitations, and escalation triggers remain visible
Required payroll, schedule, access, asset, or workflow update is confirmed
Follow-up review or reopen condition has an accountable owner

blocks.label: Final evidence, decision rationale, remaining limitation, communication, and acceptance
Log accountable review
